correctness.rationale: The new-entry event is exactly a unique absent label in the M-1 overlap, new append of that label, and independent departure of a different label. This gives the finite inclusion-exclusion flux identity. On subsequences, rare counts converge jointly to independent Poisson laws, while categories with diverging M p_i are present with probability tending to one and have vanishing M-weighted entry contributions bounded by (M p_i) exp(-M p_i). The compactified Poisson objective has interior maxima because C_k>C_(k-1). Its gradient identity, strictly increasing c/(1-exp(-c)), and strictly decreasing diagonal log derivative establish the unique maximizer. The construction attains the bound; subsequential rigidity proves the iff criterion. A standalone stdlib checker passed 2378 independent finite/rational and asymptotic sample checks; finite evidence is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The stationary rate of entries from incomplete to complete sliding windows is a natural observable of repeated coupon expiration and is distinct from target mass or first-start completion. The theorem resolves its fixed-alphabet large-window optimization at the sharp scale 1/M, classifies every asymptotically optimal sampling law uniquely up to label permutation, and shows a stark qualitative reversal from exponentially small uniform entry flux to a singular one-dominant, equal-rare allocation. The exact constants and rigidity matter precisely for optimized recurrence frequency, without asserting a downstream hitting-time result.
